newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Feb 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Feb 18.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- MERRILL BACKS DIGITAL TV CAMPAIGN WITH 1 BLN STG

Merrill Lynch, the American investment bank, is poised to launch a 1 billion pounds stg move into buying sports rights for television. It is believed that Digital Television Network, with Merrill Lynch's backing, is in talks with some Premier League football clubs about buying pay-per-view rights for top matches. The Merrill Lynch fund is part of an agreement with Digital Television Network, which is bidding for new digital channels against BSkyB, Carlton and Granada.
-- NATIONAL EXPRESS WINS CENTRAL RAIL FRANCHISE

National Express, the coach group, was yesterday handed a government subsidy of 5 stg per passenger journey to run Central Trains, the Midlands rail franchise. Central is the fifth franchise to be won by National Express and makes them the biggest train operator in the UK. The company may face competition problems as it owns an 80 per cent market share of West Midlands bus operations.
-- GULF CLOSE TO VICTORY OVER CLYDE

Gulf Canada looked to be close to victory in its 493 million stg hostile bid for Clyde Petroleum, following the acceptance of its offer by one of Clyde's four largest shareholders. Gulf reported that it now had control of 42.43 per cent of its target. Clyde is believed to have contacted a number of institutional shareholders in a last-minute attempt to convince them of its case that the management can offer far better long-term growth prospects. The 120p-per-share bid closes at 1pm today.
THE TIMES
-- LME ACCUSED OVER HAMANAKA

The chief executive of the London Metals Exchange, David King, was last night accused of misleading the copper markets over the extent of the positions built up by Yasuo Hamanaka that cost Sumitomo Corporation US$2.6 billion. Neal Wolkoff, executive vice-president of the New York Mercantile Exchange, says that King mislead the markets by saying in public in late 1995 that the high copper price was due to good, sound, fundamental economics. King told BBC1's Panorama programme last night that the LME could not reveal what it knew because it would have been a major distortional problem to the market.
-- PRIVATE INVESTORS COUNT THE COST OF GAS DEMERGER

Private investors in Centrica were left to count the cost of splitting British Gas GAS.L in two, as shares in the retail arm of British Gas fell 13.5 per cent ending its first day of official trading on the Stock Exchange at 65.25p down 10.25p. British Gas, which handles the exploration and distribution arms of the business, by contrast ended the day 2.5p higher at 174.5p.
-- LONDON CLUBS MAKES A PLAY FOR CAPITAL

London Clubs International yesterday launched a hostile share offer for Capital Corporation valuing the Crockfords and Colony Club casino group at 181 million stg. Capital Corp rejected the bid claiming that it totally failed to recognise its value. Ladbroke had also been tipped as a potential bidder. Capital shares ended the day at 186.5p yesterday up 15.5p on Friday's close.
THE GUARDIAN
-- GEORGE YIELDS ON RATE FIGHT

The Governor of the Bank of England yesterday gave up his fight to secure a rise in interest rates to combat inflationary pressures. Eddie George conceded that the speed of sterling's appreciation made it possible that core inflation would fall from its present 3.1 per cent to 2.5 per cent within three months. Although he played down the scale of the disagreement with the Chancellor, Kenneth Clarke, over a further rise in interest rates, the announcement will be a significant boost to the Cabinet morale in the run up to the general election.
-- GRANADA'S WESTBURY HOTELS SELL TO CHELSFIELD FOR 90 MLN STG

Granada is expected to announce the latest stage of its asset disposal programme with the sale of the Westbury hotels in London and New York to Chelsfield, the property group, for close to 90 million stg. The deal is likely to be followed by the sale of the Welcome Break motorway services business next week, for more than 400 million stg.
-- TELECOM TRADE DEAL PROMPTS SHARE PRICE DIP

The international telecoms market reacted yesterday to the weekend deregulation deal put together by the World Trade Organisation, when shares in international telecom companies faltered. Shares in both British Telecom and Cable & Wireless were both down by a few pence. The markets are concerned about the short-term effect on profits caused by the move to lower international call charges, but negotiators say that short-term problems will be more than offset by the growth opportunities in the medium and long term arising from liberalisation of national telecom markets.
THE INDEPENDENT

-- PENGUIN CHIEF 'DIDN'T KNOW ABOUT SCANDAL' The former head of Penguin Books in America, Peter Mayer, said yesterday that he had known nothing about the Pearson subsidiary's 100 million stg accounting scandal and had only been told of the problem a few days ago. Mayer said he was happy to help Pearson and auditor Price Waterhouse with their enquiries. City analysts took a dim view of Mayer's statements, with one saying that as chief executive he should have known.
-- POUND TEMPERS RISE IN OUTPUT AT BRITISH STEEL

Figures from British Steel, due out at the end of the month will show that its output of crude steel reached 16.12 million tons in 1996, the highest since 1989. However, the 25 per cent rise in the value of the pound over the past year has battered profitability and taken its toll on the group's share price which has fallen by almost one-third since last September.
-- TESCO TARGETS YOUNG MOTHERS

Tesco is to launch a mail order catalogue today aimed at young mothers, offering maternity clothing and nursery items including prams and pushchairs. The supermarket group is trying to win back market share lost to Mothercare, and the catalogue will offer low prices and attract bonus points on Tesco's loyalty card.
